sentences.en: In December 1968, the crew of NASA's Apollo 8 spacecraft
sentences.zh: 1968年12月，美国宇航局阿波罗8号飞船的乘组

sentences.en: became the first human beings to orbit the moon.
sentences.zh: 成为了首批环绕月球飞行的人类。

sentences.en: The astronauts on board, Frank Borman, James Lovell, and William Anders,
sentences.zh: 船上的宇航员弗兰克·博尔曼、詹姆斯·洛威尔和威廉·安德斯，

sentences.en: had a stunning view of Earth rising over the lunar horizon.
sentences.zh: 惊叹地看到地球从月球地平线上升起。

sentences.en: That Christmas Eve, a televised broadcast of the event
sentences.zh: 那年的平安夜，该事件的电视转播

sentences.en: became the most watched TV program at the time.
sentences.zh: 成为了当时收视率最高的电视节目。

sentences.en: Oh my God, look at that picture over there.
sentences.zh: 噢天哪，快看那边的那个画面。

sentences.en: William Anders captured the moment in a photograph
sentences.zh: 威廉·安德斯用一张照片捕捉到了这一刻

sentences.en: that came to be known as Earthrise.
sentences.zh: 后来这张照片被称为“地出”。

sentences.en: It showed our planet in a way people had never before seen.
sentences.zh: 它以人们从未见过的方式展现了我们的星球。

sentences.en: A vivid blue and white orb suspended against the vastness of space.
sentences.zh: 一个生动的蓝白色球体悬挂在广袤无垠的太空中。

sentences.en: Earthrise wasn't just a beautiful photograph.
sentences.zh: “地出”不仅仅是一张美丽的相片。

sentences.en: It became a symbol of the environmental movement
sentences.zh: 它成为了环保运动的象征

sentences.en: and had a profound impact on how people view our planet.
sentences.zh: 并对人们看待我们星球的方式产生了深远的影响。

sentences.en: Beautiful, but fragile and deserving of our protection.
sentences.zh: 美丽，但脆弱，值得我们去保护。

sentences.en: The picture inspired the launch of Earth Day.
sentences.zh: 这张照片启发了地球日的发起。

sentences.en: It's a global movement that is still around decades later.
sentences.zh: 这是一个至今仍然存在的全球性运动。

sentences.en: It involves billions of people around the world.
sentences.zh: 它吸引了全世界数十亿人的参与。

sentences.en: All of this inspired by a simple, beautiful image.
sentences.zh: 所有这一切都源于一个简单而美丽的画面。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, the power of beauty.
sentences.zh: 本周的“隐藏的大脑”，美的力量。

sentences.en: Why we are so moved by it, the ways it influences our behavior,
sentences.zh: 为什么我们会被它深深打动，它影响我们行为的方式，

sentences.en: and how our attraction to beauty might unlock the secrets of the universe.
sentences.zh: 以及我们对美的向往如何能够解开宇宙的奥秘。

sentences.en: In the early 1990s, Anjan Chatterjee was a young neuroscientist
sentences.zh: 20世纪90年代初，安扬·查特吉是一名年轻的神经科学家

sentences.en: working at the University of Birmingham in Alabama.
sentences.zh: 在阿拉巴马州的伯明翰大学工作。

sentences.en: On Fridays, Anjan and two colleagues would get together at a local hangout
sentences.zh: 每逢周五，安扬和两位同事会聚在当地的一个常去场所

sentences.en: to talk about work and life.
And the place we got together was a bar
sentences.zh: 我们聚会的地方是一个酒吧

sentences.en: that was close to across the street from where I lived in Birmingham
sentences.zh: 它离我在伯明翰住的地方差不多隔了一条街

sentences.en: And just to set the scene, this is one of these beautiful central courtyards
sentences.zh: 为了营造一下氛围，这是一个美丽的中央庭院，

sentences.en: with architectural remnants and wrought iron chairs and magnolia trees.
sentences.zh: 里面有建筑遗迹、熟铁椅子和木兰树。

sentences.en: An aesthetically pleasing place to be talking about ideas and talking about life.
sentences.zh: 这是一个适合畅谈思想和生活的赏心悦目之地。

sentences.en: One evening, as they sat under the magnolia trees sipping their drinks,
sentences.zh: 一天晚上，当他们坐在木兰树下啜饮着饮品时，

sentences.en: Anjan's friend Britt posed a question.
sentences.zh: 安扬的朋友布里特提出了一个问题。

sentences.en: Imagine yourself 10 years in the future.
sentences.zh: 想象一下十年后的自己。

sentences.en: What would you regret that you hadn't done
sentences.zh: 回顾过去，你会为自己没有在工作上

sentences.en: with respect to your work looking backwards?
Britt was fond of asking these meta questions.
sentences.zh: 布里特很喜欢问这种元问题。

sentences.en: And it was a nice way, because there was also going to be a transition in my life.
sentences.zh: 这是一种很好的方式，因为我的生活也将迎来一个转变。

sentences.en: I was going to move to a new place, new lab,
sentences.zh: 我将搬到一个新的地方、新的实验室，

sentences.en: to also generally reevaluate how I wanted to direct my attention.
sentences.zh: 同时也全面重新评估我想如何引导自己的注意力。

sentences.en: Anjan knew the answer to his friend's question.
sentences.zh: 安扬知道朋友这个问题的答案。

sentences.en: He had always been interested in art.
sentences.zh: 他一直对艺术很感兴趣。

sentences.en: As a young boy growing up in India,
sentences.zh: 作为一个在印度长大的小男孩，

sentences.en: he spent many hours drawing pictures of landscapes,
sentences.zh: 他花了很多时间画风景画，
琢磨是什么让它们变得美丽。

sentences.en: Anjan was still interested in that question.
sentences.zh: 安扬依然对这个问题很感兴趣。

sentences.en: He wanted to understand the science of aesthetics.
sentences.zh: 他想要了解审美的科学。

sentences.en: Why are we drawn to beautiful things?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们会被美丽的事物所吸引？

sentences.en: And how does the mind process beauty?
sentences.zh: 大脑又是如何处理美的？

sentences.en: what happens in the minds of artists when they produce beautiful works?
sentences.zh: 当艺术家创作精美作品时，他们的大脑中会发生什么？

sentences.en: When I started to look at this in the late 90s,
sentences.zh: 当我在90年代末开始研究这个课题时，

sentences.en: there was virtually nothing written about it from the point of view of neuroscience.
sentences.zh: 从神经科学的角度来看，几乎没有任何相关的著作。

sentences.en: There are many ways to study these questions,
sentences.zh: 研究这些问题的方法有很多，

sentences.en: but one technique is to observe patients who have suffered some kind of neurological damage.
sentences.zh: 但其中一种技术是观察遭受某种神经损伤的患者。

sentences.en: Anjan began studying artists who had different neurological deficits,
sentences.zh: 安扬开始研究患有不同神经系统功能障碍的艺术家，

sentences.en: to see what effect it had on their art.
sentences.zh: 以观察它对他们的艺术创作产生了什么影响。

sentences.en: If a stroke or a brain disorder changes the way people perceive or produce art,
sentences.zh: 如果中风或脑部疾病改变了人们感知或创作艺术的方式，

sentences.en: it tells you that the affected area was playing a role in aesthetics.
sentences.zh: 这就说明受损区域在审美中发挥了一定作用。

sentences.en: In some rare cases, Anjan says,
sentences.zh: 安扬表示，在某些罕见情况下，

sentences.en: brain damage seems to enhance people's capacity for art.
sentences.zh: 脑损伤似乎能增强人们的艺术能力。

sentences.en: It's a paradox because, on the one hand,
sentences.zh: 这是一个悖论，因为一方面，

sentences.en: you might think that art is the highest expression of our humanity.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为艺术是我们人性最高级的表达。

sentences.en: we don't ever talk about how someone's language gets better.
sentences.zh: 我们从来不会去讨论某人的语言能力是如何变好的。

sentences.en: We don't talk about how their emotional processing

或决策能力是如何变好的。

sentences.en: And yet, here, in some instances,

sentences.en: people can have brain damage or neurologic disease,
sentences.zh: 人们可能会遭受脑损伤或神经系统疾病，

sentences.en: and their art changes and changes in a way that some people find more appealing.
sentences.zh: 而他们的艺术会发生改变，并且这种改变在某些人看来更具吸引力。

sentences.en: The point is not that if you get brain damage,
sentences.zh: 重点并不是说如果你得了脑损伤，
你的艺术就会变得更好，

sentences.zh: 但在某些情况下，确实会发生这种情况。

and in the experience of pleasure.
